short: Sixteen valves on a four-cylinder engine: two intake and two exhaust valves for each cylinder.
Two-wheel drive: only one pair of wheels is driven.
ZF’s eight-speed automatic, whose valve body and TCM form one mechatronic unit.

example.text: On the 9HP the TCM is a separate module bolted to the case, not built into the valve body as on the 8HP.

short: Chrysler’s version of the ZF nine-speed, built under license; its service information is often used for the 9HP.

example.text: FCA issued a bulletin on the C-clutch snap ring in early 948TE units, and a half-seated ring here can destroy the transmission.

short: ZF’s transverse nine-speed automatic in the Discovery Sport, built from four planetary sets and two dog clutches.

example.text: There is no bottom pan on the 9HP48; this side cover is the only way into the controls.

short: The updated successor to the 9HP48, used in the Discovery Sport from the 2020 model year.
Air conditioning, the system that cools the cabin.

example.text: Have the A/C system evacuated with a recovery machine before any refrigerant line is opened.

short: The belt-driven pump that compresses refrigerant to make the air conditioning work.

example.text: Bolt the A/C compressor back onto its mounting on the LH side.

short: The add-on units an engine drives with a belt, such as the unit that charges the battery and the air conditioning compressor.
The ribbed rubber belt on the front of the engine that drives the accessories from the crankshaft.

example.text: Refit each idler pulley to its noted position and fit the accessory belt.

short: A part that turns an electrical command into movement, such as opening a valve.

example.text: Unplug every sensor, actuator and injector connector, release the harness clips and brackets, and lift the engine harness off as one piece.

short: Values a TCM learns as it runs, such as clutch fill times and pressures, so shifts stay smooth as parts wear.

example.text: Adaptations are learned clutch fill times and pressures; old values from worn parts give harsh or flared shifts on the new packs.

short: Made or sold by a company other than the vehicle maker, as many rebuild kits are.

example.text: Fit Subaru's updated valve body, or rebuild the worn bores with aftermarket valve and sleeve kits if you have the tooling.

short: The box at the start of the intake that holds the engine air filter.

example.text: Take out the air intake duct and boot, the rear air cleaner case and the radiator.

short: Blowing regulated shop air into a clutch circuit to hear and feel the piston apply, and to find leaks.
Temporary pins screwed into bolt holes to guide a part straight into place.

example.text: Clip the injectors to the rail, guide the assembly in on the JLR guide pins, and tighten the rail bolts one turn at a time.

short: Steel rod threaded along its whole length, used to make pulling and pressing tools.
The belt-driven unit that makes electricity to charge the battery while the engine runs.
long: Subaru steps call it the generator.

example.text: Disconnect the battery cable and connector, remove the two bolts and lift off the generator.

short: Smaller bolt-on parts on an engine, such as sensors, brackets and pipes.
A dial fitted between a wrench and a socket that shows how many degrees a bolt has been turned.

example.text: Set the RH half onto the LH half, lightly oil the joining bolt threads and washers, fit the bolts, and screw in two head bolts where shown to anchor the angle gauge.

short: Tightening a bolt to a set torque, then turning it a further set number of degrees.
long: Turning by angle stretches the bolt by a known amount, so the clamping force is far more consistent than a torque reading alone, which friction can fool.

example.text: With the locking tools still fitted, tighten both VCT center bolts to torque and then the final angle.

short: Another name for the ring gear of a planetary gear set.

example.text: Install the gear 4 annulus and pinion carrier assembly.

short: Packaging that protects electronic parts, such as a TCM, from damage by static electricity.

example.text: Unplug and unbolt the transmission control module from the outside of the case and store it in anti-static packaging.

short: The first plate in a clutch pack, the one the piston pushes on.

example.text: With a resealed piston, lay in the apply plate, then alternate steel and friction four times, then the pressure plate and snap ring.

short: A bench press with a lever-driven ram, used to press parts together or apart and to compress springs.

example.text: In an arbor press, compress the D piston retainer with the press tool and adapter and remove its snap ring.

short: A sticky lubricant that holds sealing rings and washers in place during assembly and dissolves in fluid.

example.text: Coat the stator support rings with assembly gel, then lower the bell housing over the stack, rotating the output support and E clutch slightly until the guide pins enter their holes.

short: A thick lubricant put on rubbing parts during assembly to protect them until the oil reaches them.

example.text: The first oil carries assembly lube and machining debris.

short: After top dead center: a crankshaft position given in degrees past TDC.

example.text: That is 50 degrees after TDC on cylinder 1.

short: The oil-like fluid that fills an automatic transmission; each design needs its own exact type.
long: Short for automatic transmission fluid.

example.text: Topping up with a generic multi-vehicle ATF.

short: An extra electric pump some transmissions use to keep up fluid pressure while the engine is stopped.
Active Valve Control System: Subaru’s name for its oil-driven cam phasers.

example.text: New bearings, the chain tensioners and the AVCS sprockets all need oil before the engine fires.

short: A drive layout in which the engine drives both the front and the rear wheels.
long: Short for all-wheel drive.

example.text: The US Discovery Sport is AWD, so the PTU is splined into the differential and must come away before the transmission can drop.

short: Movement along a shaft’s axis; for a whole shaft this is the same as end play.

example.text: Check the turbo shaft for radial and axial play, wheel contact and coked oil in the center housing, and confirm the oil feed and return pipes are clear.

short: A shaft that carries drive from the transmission to a wheel.
long: The front ones are also called halfshafts.

example.text: With the vehicle supported, remove the front halfshafts and separate the power transfer unit from the transmission's differential side.

short: The lip seal where an axle enters the transmission or differential.

example.text: Drive out and discard the differential seals from both the case and the bell housing.

short: To loosen a bolt, nut or tool a little, either to release it or as a planned step in tightening.

example.text: Apply a 3 mm sealant bead where shown, fit a new gasket and the cover, then tighten, back off and retighten every bolt.

short: The small free movement between meshing gear teeth before one starts to drive the other.

example.text: If the hypoid gears, bearings or case were replaced, pinion depth and backlash must be re-set before going further.

short: A plate that stops oil or fluid sloshing away from the pickup.

example.text: Bolt the pan baffle back on, then install a new oil strainer with a new O-ring.

short: A pair of weighted shafts, geared to the crankshaft, that spin to cancel the shaking an inline four makes.

example.text: Out-of-phase balancers add vibration instead of canceling it, and their timing cannot be set once the crank is in.

short: The free-turning gear that passes drive from the crankshaft to the balance shafts.

example.text: Remove the balancer idler gear, then withdraw both counter-rotating balancer shafts from their bores in the block.

short: A hollow bolt with a side hole that carries oil through a ring-shaped pipe end, sealed by a washer on each side.

example.text: Banjo bolts and washers on the oil feed are single use; a reused washer is a common source of oil leaks onto a hot turbo.

short: One row of cylinders; a boxer has two, one on each side.

example.text: Counting links instead of matching the colored links is the usual way the LH bank ends up a tooth off.

short: As a unit, a metric measure of pressure equal to 100 kPa, about 14.5 psi.

example.text: Reusing an HP line that has already been tightened its maximum number of times, which risks a fuel leak at 200 bar.

short: The round part of a cam lobe, where the valve stays closed.

example.text: With each lobe on its base circle, measure between the cam and the roller with a feeler gauge and record every reading.

short: A power supply that holds the battery voltage steady while new software is loaded into a control module.

example.text: Connect a battery support unit and the JLR diagnostic tool, update the TCM to the latest calibration, then run the TCM configuration routine, entering the transmission serial number when asked.

short: A continuous line of sealant laid along a face, sized by its thickness in millimeters.

example.text: Run a small bead of liquid gasket along the chamfer edge of the cover, skipping the marked oil hole.

short: A part that supports a turning or sliding shaft so it moves with little friction or wear.
long: Most engine bearings are plain bearings: smooth half-round strips of soft metal that a shaft spins in on a thin layer of oil. Transmissions also use bearings with balls, rollers or needles. Bearings are meant to wear instead of the costly parts around them, so a rebuild replaces them.

example.text: Set the front differential into the converter case on its bearings.

short: The half-round cradle machined in the block that holds a main bearing shell.

example.text: Lay the grooved upper main shells, with their oil holes lined up, into the clean, dry block saddles.

short: One half of a plain bearing: a thin steel strip lined with soft bearing metal and curved into a half circle.
long: Two shells make a round bearing. They are thin and soft on purpose, so dirt embeds in them instead of scratching the shaft, and they are replaced at a rebuild.

example.text: Bearing shells are chosen from these codes and the selection charts, not just from measuring.

short: The bell-shaped front section of the transmission that surrounds the torque converter and bolts to the engine.

example.text: The converter must come off first; the bell housing cannot be split with it in place.

short: A dished steel disc spring that returns a clutch piston; it is so strongly loaded that it must be compressed in a press.

example.text: The Belleville spring is under heavy load; the retainer only moves about an eighth of an inch.

short: A spring-loaded arm with a pulley that keeps the accessory belt tight.

example.text: Turn the belt tensioner clockwise with a wrench to relieve tension and slip the belt off, then remove the belt tensioner and the idler pulley.

short: A stand that holds a transmission steady on the bench while it is worked on.

example.text: Stand the CVT securely on a bench fixture, then degrease the outside, especially the chain cover seam and bell housing, before any cover comes off.

short: The large bottom eye of a connecting rod, split so it can be clamped around the crankshaft.

example.text: Letting the rod's big end drag along the bore scratches the liner; guide it out by hand.

short: To let trapped air or pressure out of a system, such as air from the cooling system or pressure from the fuel lines.

example.text: Bleed fuel pressure using the factory procedure, remove the fuel filler cap to vent the tank, then disconnect the battery ground.

short: A hole with a closed bottom; liquid trapped in a threaded one can stop a bolt seating or crack the part.

example.text: Coolant or oil left in a blind hole gives a false torque reading and can crack the block.

short: The two sides of a boxer engine’s block, split down the middle and bolted together around the crankshaft.

example.text: Lay Plastigage on each journal, join the block halves with oiled bolts and run the full joining-bolt torque sequence, then split the halves and read each strip.

short: Combustion gas that leaks past the piston rings into the crankcase.

example.text: Staggered gaps limit blow-by, and no gap may sit in line with the piston skirt.

short: Blue or straw-colored marks on steel parts, such as gears and bearings, that show they have been overheated.

example.text: Look at all four sheave faces for scoring, steps, galling or bluing where the chain runs.

short: A precisely machined round hole: most often a cylinder, but also any hole that a shaft, pin or valve runs in.

example.text: Pulling the rail down on one bolt and cocking an injector in its bore.

short: A dial indicator on a long handle with a sensing foot, used to read a bore’s size at different depths and directions.

example.text: With the chosen shells fitted and the caps torqued, check main and rod clearances with Plastigage or a bore gauge and compare them with the selection chart.

short: Machining a cylinder larger and truly round again so oversize pistons can be fitted.

example.text: Boring the liners oversize on the assumption that oversize pistons will be available leaves a block with no factory pistons to fit it.

short: A large German parts maker; it supplies the fuel injectors and their seal kits.

example.text: JLR warns that the Bosch sheet in the refit kit gives the steps in the wrong order.

short: A raised, thickened spot on a casting or part that carries a bolt hole or a shaft.

example.text: Press the transfer gear bearing back onto its case boss.

short: The lower part of an engine: the crankshaft, rods and bearings, and the block around them.

example.text: The tray stiffens the bottom end and covers the main caps and rod caps.

short: A thread tap with only a very short lead at its tip, so it cleans threads right to the bottom of a blind hole.

example.text: Clean all threads, including the drive plate holes with an M10 x 1.0 bottoming tap no deeper than the hole, then wash the block and head and blow them dry.

short: An engine whose cylinders lie flat in two opposite rows, so the pistons move in and out toward each other like boxers’ fists.
A clutch pack whose outer plates are splined to the case, so applying it holds part of the gear train still.

example.text: Remove the D brake plates and frictions, keeping them in order.

short: A round chamber behind the brake pedal that uses engine vacuum to add force to the driver’s push.

example.text: Reconnect fuel and evaporation lines, heater and booster hoses, the A/C line, harness connectors, radiator and intake ducting.

short: One of the small oil-filled units in the CVVL that controls one intake valve and also acts as its lash adjuster.

example.text: The brake units also act as the intake valve lash adjusters and must start from the reset position.

short: The first miles of gentle driving while the piston rings seat and new surfaces wear in together.

example.text: Rings seat and new parts settle during this period; Subaru notes some oil use is normal while an engine is breaking in.

short: A pipe or hose that carries crankcase gas out to the ventilation system.

example.text: Install the coolant pipes, degas bottle, breather, purge valve, dipstick tube and NVH pads with new or inspected O-rings.

short: Dents pressed into a bearing race, often from pushing a bearing on by the wrong ring.

example.text: Pressing on the outer race brinells a new bearing.

short: The wall between the engine bay and the cabin; wiring passes through it at special connectors.

example.text: Tag and unplug the bulkhead harness connectors, generator and A/C compressor leads, and the engine ground strap; free the harness from its clips.

short: A plain bearing in the form of a tube, pressed into a bore.

example.text: The converter hub runs in a bearing, not a bushing, so check it for roughness while it is exposed.

short: A tube that keeps fluid pressure available so the transmission can drive off at once when the engine restarts after an auto stop.

example.text: The bypass tube gives instant pressure on restart after an auto stop; a leak here shows as slow drive-away.

short: A spring-loaded valve that lets oil flow around a clogged filter so the engine is never left without oil.

example.text: Fitting the filter cap without checking that the bypass valve is clipped in.

short: A C-shaped clip that locks an axle into the differential; always fit new ones when the axles come out.

example.text: Subaru treats the axle C-clips as one-time use.

short: The ring that holds a rolling bearing’s balls or rollers evenly spaced.

example.text: The bearing blocks the D piston housing, so it must come off first; pulling on the cage ruins it.

short: The software and settings loaded into a control module; updating it can change how the engine or transmission behaves.

example.text: Many 9HP shift complaints were cured by calibration updates rather than parts; a rebuild will not fix a software complaint.

short: A sliding measuring tool with jaws; quick to use, but less precise than a micrometer.
A small cap that bolts over a camshaft journal; each one must go back in its own place.

example.text: Prying on the unsupported lower corner of a cam carrier cracks the cam cap and scraps the whole carrier.

short: A machined frame bolted on top of the head that holds the camshafts in their bearings.
long: On the Subaru engine the carrier and its caps are machined together, so they are replaced as a set. On both engines the camshafts lift out with the carrier.

example.text: Remove the nineteen bolts and lift the camshaft carrier, with both camshafts inside it, off the head.

short: One of the egg-shaped bumps on a camshaft; its height sets how far the valve opens.

example.text: Setting the carrier with a lobe on a rocker can bend a valve or crack the carrier.

short: An oil-driven hub on the end of a camshaft that turns it slightly ahead or behind, changing valve timing while the engine runs.

example.text: Each VCT actuator is matched to its camshaft, and the two are not interchangeable.

short: A shaft with egg-shaped bumps that open the valves as it turns; the crankshaft drives it at half its own speed.

example.text: Turn each camshaft until its mark points up and bolt the camshaft setting tool across both.

short: A sensor that reads a target on a camshaft so the engine computer knows where each cam is.

example.text: Install both camshaft position sensors with new O-rings.

short: A removable half-round piece that bolts over a shaft’s journal to hold it in its bearing.
A bolt held loosely in its part so it cannot fall out when the part is removed.

example.text: Loosen the captive bolts and lift off the engine vent oil separator, discarding its gasket.

short: A word with three meanings: the frame holding an engine’s camshafts, the frame holding a gear set’s small orbiting gears, or a differential’s housing.

example.text: The camshafts run in the carrier, not in the head.

short: A measure of volume, one cubic centimeter; 1,000 of them make a liter, and engine size is often given this way.
The middle section of a turbocharger, which holds the shaft’s oil-fed bearings.

example.text: Check the turbo shaft for radial and axial play, wheel contact and coked oil in the center housing, and confirm the oil feed and return pipes are clear.

short: The single large bolt that holds a cam phaser on the end of its camshaft.

example.text: Break both VCT actuator center bolts loose but leave them threaded in.

short: A cover that encloses a chain drive and keeps the oil in around it.

example.text: A timing error found now costs minutes; found after the chain cover is sealed it costs the cover.

short: A rail with a plastic wear face that a chain slides along, keeping it on its path.

example.text: Unbolt the LH chain guide and lift off the LH timing chain.

short: The variator chain sliding on the pulley sheaves instead of gripping, which damages the chain and pulleys together.

example.text: Subaru's own fix for confirmed chain slip is a complete CVT, and loose pulleys and chains are hard to source.

short: Wear in a chain’s pins and joints that makes it longer, which makes the cam timing late.
A spring- and oil-loaded plunger that presses on a chain, usually through a pivoting arm, to keep it tight.

example.text: Remove the two bolts and the primary chain tensioner.

short: A CVT that uses a steel chain, rather than a steel push band, between its pulleys.
A small angled edge cut where two faces meet, such as around the mouth of a bore.

example.text: Run a small bead of liquid gasket along the chamfer edge of the cover, skipping the marked oil hole.

short: Running a tap or thread chaser through existing threads to clean them without cutting new metal.
A small ball in a valve body passage that lets fluid flow one way only.

example.text: Pulling the wrong bolts splits the valve body on the bench and scatters check balls and springs.

short: A plug set at the correct fluid height; with the fluid hot and the engine running, fluid is added until it just runs out.

example.text: With the engine idling in Park, watch the fluid temperature on the diagnostic tool and set the level at the check plug while it is inside the temperature window in the service data.

short: A small snap ring that sits in a groove; on a piston, two of them stop the piston pin sliding out.

example.text: Remove both circlips, push out the piston pin and separate each piston from its rod.

short: The squeezing force a tightened bolt actually puts on a joint.

example.text: Loosening in sequence keeps the head from distorting as clamp load comes off.

short: The small designed gap between two parts that move against each other, often measured in hundredths of a millimeter.

example.text: Measure each valve stem tip and the bore of its shim and confirm the clearance between them.

short: A device that locks two turning parts together on command and releases them again.

example.text: Holding the E plates in their hub, set the E clutch and hub onto the output gear support.

short: A stack of alternating friction and steel plates in a drum, squeezed by a piston to lock two parts together.

example.text: Lifting by the hub pulls it out of the B clutch pack and drops the plates.

short: The piston that fluid pressure pushes to squeeze a clutch pack.

example.text: Compress the E Belleville spring, remove its retainer, then lift the bonded piston out of the steel drum.

short: Oil that heat has baked into hard carbon, common inside a turbocharger after hot shutdowns.

example.text: Check the turbo shaft for radial and axial play, wheel contact and coked oil in the center housing, and confirm the oil feed and return pipes are clear.

short: Two small half-cone pieces that lock a valve spring retainer to the valve stem.
long: Also called keepers.

example.text: Compress each spring, remove the collets, then the retainer, spring, valve and spring seat, keeping each valve's parts together.

short: Links of a different color on a new timing chain that line up with the timing marks on the sprockets.
long: Matching colors to marks is far more reliable than counting links, which is how a chain usually ends up a tooth out.

example.text: The colored links are the only reference for chain-to-sprocket timing.

short: The space above the piston at the top of its travel, where the fuel and air burn.
Air from a shop compressor, used to blow out passages and to test fluid circuits.

example.text: Blow every head bolt hole in the block clean and dry with compressed air.

short: The squeezing of the air and fuel as the piston rises, and the pressure this builds.

example.text: Pulling the plugs lets the crank turn freely without compression while the timing is set up.

short: How many times the space above a piston shrinks from the bottom of its stroke to the top, such as 10.5 to 1.
One of the upper piston rings, which seal combustion pressure above the piston.

example.text: Upside-down compression rings pump oil into the chamber, the same symptom behind Subaru's FB oil consumption bulletins.

short: The strong link that joins a piston to the crankshaft.
Short metal tubes with O-rings that carry fluid between the valve body and passages in the case.

example.text: Remove the valve body connecting tubes and the filter bypass tube, noting which are round and which have one oblong end.

short: A plug and socket that join wires, so a part can be unplugged.

example.text: Reconnect the main harness connector and bolt the top cover back on.

short: A plastic frame on the valve body that carries the wiring to its solenoids and sensors.

example.text: Label every solenoid and photograph the connector plate routing before anything is unplugged.

short: The ring where a valve face actually touches its seat; its width and position are checked.

example.text: The contact band should sit in the middle of the valve face; a wide or off-center band means the seats need cutting.

short: The smooth neck on the back of a torque converter that turns in its seal and drives the pump.

example.text: The converter hub runs in a bearing, not a bushing, so check it for roughness while it is exposed.

short: The lip seal at the front of the transmission that the converter hub turns in.

example.text: Remove the snap ring and drive out the converter hub seal; check the hub support bearing.

short: A bracket that holds the torque converter in the transmission while the engine and transmission are apart.

example.text: Remove the starter, attach the torque converter stopper to the converter housing, then remove the upper transmission-to-engine bolts.

short: The mix of water and antifreeze that carries heat away from the engine.

example.text: Pull the side-mounted oil pan drain plug and drain the oil, then drain any coolant left in the block and pipes.

short: The metal pipes and hoses that carry coolant around the engine.
long: Subaru calls them water pipes.

example.text: Unbolt the coolant pipes and hoses around the engine and remove the coolant degas separator, checking each O-ring as it comes out.

short: The pipes and hoses that carry transmission fluid to and from its cooler.

example.text: Refit the crossmember, axles with new C-clips, propeller shaft, cooler lines and harness, flushing the cooler circuit first.

short: A Subaru additive put into the cooling system when it is refilled after engine work.

example.text: Add the cooling system conditioner and fill with Subaru Super Coolant.

short: Turning in opposite directions, like two shafts geared together.

example.text: Remove the balancer idler gear, then withdraw both counter-rotating balancer shafts from their bores in the block.

short: A bolted lid that closes an opening in an engine or transmission and usually seals it.

example.text: Fit the cover and tighten its ten bolts in a crossing pattern.

short: Inspecting a part for cracks, by eye and with dye penetrant, before deciding whether to reuse it.

example.text: Crack-check the crank, check runout on the end journals with a dial gauge, and mic every main journal and crank pin for size, taper and out-of-round.

short: The flat rear end of the crankshaft that the drive plate bolts to.

example.text: Pushing the seal over the crank flange without its spacer and rolling the lip.

short: One of the offset journals on a crankshaft that a connecting rod’s big end turns on.

example.text: Letting the rod's big end strike the crank pin or liner on the way in nicks both.

short: The pulley on the front of the crankshaft that drives the accessory belt; it often has a rubber-mounted damper ring.

example.text: Lock the crank pulley with the pulley wrench and pin set, break the bolt loose and remove the bolt and pulley.

short: A special tool for turning the crankshaft by hand from the front of the engine.

example.text: Fit the crank rotation tool and turn the crankshaft clockwise only until the pulley mark points down and both cam marks point up.

short: A lip seal at either end of the crankshaft that keeps oil in where the shaft leaves the engine.

example.text: The rear crank seal and the lower timing cover sit behind the drive plate.

short: The space inside the block below the pistons, where the crankshaft turns.
Drawing blow-by gas out of the crankcase and into the intake, so it is burned instead of building up pressure.
The main shaft of the engine, turned by the pistons through their rods; it drives the transmission.
long: Offset sections along it turn the up-and-down push of each piston into rotation, the way pedals turn a bicycle crank.

example.text: Oil the main journals and lower the crankshaft into the LH half.

short: The front end of the crankshaft, which carries the sprocket and pulley.

example.text: Slide the crank sprocket off the crankshaft nose.

short: A sensor that reads a toothed ring on the crankshaft or drive plate to report engine speed and position.

example.text: Fit the crankshaft position sensor to the lower timing cover, where it reads the drive plate reluctor ring.

short: A Subaru special socket that fits the crankshaft nose so the engine can be turned by hand.

example.text: Turn the crank clockwise with the crankshaft socket until the crank sprocket and the RH intake and exhaust sprocket marks line up, with the crank key at six o'clock.

short: A strong beam across the underside of the car that the engine or transmission mounts bolt to.

example.text: From underneath, remove the front exhaust pipe and the lower transmission-to-engine bolts and nuts, then remove the nuts holding the engine mounts to the crossmember.

short: A slightly dished or wavy plate in a clutch pack that softens the engagement.

example.text: Remove the housing support bolts, then lift out the reverse brake plates in order, noting which way the dished cushion plate faces.

short: Continuously variable transmission: instead of fixed gears, it changes its ratio smoothly to any value in its range.

example.text: Fill the CVT through the filler plug with the specified fluid, temporarily refit the plug and start the engine.

short: The special fluid a CVT needs so its chain grips properly.
long: Short for CVT fluid.

example.text: Fit new sealing rings on the pulley shafts and input shaft and lubricate them with CVTF.

short: Subaru’s green CVT fluid, the one specified for the CVT in this app.
Continuously variable valve lift: JLR’s oil-filled unit between the intake cam and the intake valves that varies how far and how long they open.
long: The cam pushes small pistons that pressurize oil instead of pushing the valves, and solenoids decide how much of that oil reaches each valve. It cannot be repaired, must stay upright, and needs clean oil of the right type.

example.text: JLR warns that oil outside its specification can make the CVVL system malfunction.

short: One of the round, straight-walled chambers in an engine where fuel and air are burned.

example.text: With the spark plugs out and fuel injection disabled, check compression on all four cylinders and record the numbers.

short: The main casting of an engine, which contains the cylinders.

example.text: Bolt the structural windage tray to the bottom of the block.

short: The casting bolted on top of the cylinders that closes them off and holds the valves.

example.text: With a helper, lower the head straight onto the dowels.

short: A hard iron tube in an aluminum block that forms the cylinder wall the piston slides on.

example.text: Check each thin-wall cast-iron liner for scoring, cracks and any movement at the deck.

short: How close a bore or journal is to a perfect cylinder along its whole length; it combines taper and out-of-round.
The flat machined top of the block, or the matching underside of the head, where the two seal together.

example.text: The bore size grade (A or B) is stamped on the block deck and decides which piston grade belongs in each hole.

short: The height of a block or head measured to its deck; machining the deck reduces it, so there is a minimum.

example.text: Have the decks resurfaced only if they are past the warpage limit, and never below the minimum block height.

short: A block whose sides reach down past the crankshaft’s center line, which makes it stiffer.
The coolant tank where air bubbles separate out of the cooling system.

example.text: Install the coolant pipes, degas bottle, breather, purge valve, dipstick tube and NVH pads with new or inspected O-rings.

short: The unit for measuring angles: a full turn is 360 of them, and half a turn is 180.

example.text: The pump body seats only one way; turned 180 degrees, it will not sit down.

short: A spring-loaded notch that holds a lever firmly in each of its positions.
A connecting rod whose cap is split at an angle, so the big end is narrow enough to pass up through the bore.

example.text: The FB has no piston pin service holes; its diagonally split rods let the piston and rod leave through the bore once the head is off.

short: A gauge with a spring-loaded tip and a needle on a dial that shows very small movements.
long: Also called a dial gauge.

example.text: Check crankshaft end play with a dial indicator and turn the crank by hand to confirm it spins freely.

short: A gear set that drives two axles while letting them turn at different speeds in corners.

example.text: Lift the differential assembly out of the case.

short: The marked rod that dips into the oil to show its level.
long: Subaru calls it the oil level gauge.

example.text: Fill with 0W-20 synthetic oil through the filler to the F mark on the dipstick.

short: Spraying fuel straight into the combustion chamber at very high pressure.
The total volume all the pistons sweep through in one stroke each; the usual measure of engine size.
A clutch that locks two parts with interlocking teeth instead of friction; it cannot slip, so it must engage at matched speeds.
long: The nine-speed in this app has two, called A and F, because they waste no energy while open. They are its best-known weak point.

example.text: Dog clutch engagements need several cycles before shifts settle.

short: The sensor that tells the TCM when a dog clutch has finished moving.

example.text: Power the dog clutch pressure sensor from a bench supply and apply air to confirm its output changes; an ohmmeter will not test it.

short: Double overhead camshafts: two camshafts in each cylinder head, one for the intake valves and one for the exhaust valves.
A piston that fluid pushes in both directions, through separate apply and release passages.

example.text: Remove the output gear nut, bearing and gear from the support, then remove the F dog sleeve and its double-acting piston and cover.

short: A short, precise pin that lines up two parts so they always bolt together in the same place.
long: Subaru calls them knock pins.

example.text: Raise the unit, engage the dowels, and torque the transmission-to-engine bolts.

short: A threaded plug at the lowest point of an engine or transmission, removed to let the oil or fluid out.

example.text: Open the filler cap, drain the oil from the pan, refit the drain plug with a new gasket and spin off the oil filter.

short: The small gear that drives the differential’s ring gear.

example.text: Remove the pinion support bolts and pry the support up with the drive pinion, saving the two seals.

short: A thin steel disc bolted to the back of the crankshaft that drives the torque converter and carries teeth for the starter.
long: Cars with a stick shift have a heavy flywheel here instead.

example.text: The stopper must be out before the converter can be pulled up to the drive plate.

short: The shafts and joints that carry drive from the transmission to the wheels.
A cup-shaped part that turns on a shaft and holds a stack of plates inside it.

example.text: Install the input shaft with the forward drum and clutch pack into the case.

short: A pump with two pumping chambers, so it delivers fluid twice in each turn.
A solenoid switched on and off many times a second; the share of time it is on sets the pressure it lets through.
A crack test: a bright dye soaks into any crack, then a white developer draws it back out so the crack shows.

example.text: Look over the heads and block for cracks and use dye penetrant on the critical areas, and check gasket faces for gas or water tracks.

short: Exhaust gas recirculation: feeding a little exhaust back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and emissions.

example.text: Fit the EGR pipe to the water pipe and RH block half with a new gasket.

short: Subaru’s older boxer engine family, used before the current engines.
Controlled electrically but worked by oil: solenoids steer pressurized oil, and the oil moves the parts.
How far a shaft can slide back and forth along its own length.
long: Also called end float.

example.text: Check the input shaft end play and that the shaft turns with slight resistance.

short: The moment a clutch takes up the drive, felt as the car going into gear.

example.text: Accepting a loose pack, which slips and burns on engagement.

short: The machine that burns fuel and air to turn a shaft and power the car.

example.text: Revving the engine right after first start.

short: A bracket bolted to the engine for a hoist chain to hook onto.

example.text: Fit new O-rings, install the water pipe and PCV connector set, then the rear engine hanger.

short: A wheeled frame with a long lifting arm and a chain, used to lift an engine in and out of the car.

example.text: Hang the engine from a hoist with chains or wire rope and put a jack under the transmission.

short: Rubber-and-metal blocks that hold the engine in the car and soak up its vibration.

example.text: Bolt the engine mounts on, then sling the engine and remove it from the stand.

short: A steel frame on wheels with a turning mount that bolts to an engine, so it can be rolled over while you work.

example.text: Bolt the engine to a stand using the JLR engine stand adapter so it can be rotated for top and bottom access.

short: A bar laid across the engine bay that holds the engine up while the transmission is removed.
Pumping the refrigerant out of the A/C system with a machine, and later refilling it with the right amount.

example.text: Have the A/C system evacuated with a recovery machine before any refrigerant line is opened.

short: A hose that carries fuel vapor from the tank so it can be burned in the engine instead of escaping.

example.text: Reconnect fuel and evaporation lines, heater and booster hoses, the A/C line, harness connectors, radiator and intake ducting.

short: The burned gas leaving the cylinders, and the outlet side of the engine that carries it away.

example.text: Swapping the intake and exhaust phasers on reassembly.

short: The passages that collect exhaust from each cylinder; some engines have it cast into the cylinder head.

example.text: The exhaust manifold is cast into the head, so the turbo bolts straight to the head and must come off before the head can.

short: A section bolted to the back of the transmission case that covers the rear output.
long: Subaru calls it the extension case.

example.text: With a new transfer clutch O-ring and fresh sealant, fit the extension case and torque its bolts in a crossing pattern.

short: A pipe outside the transmission case that carries pressurized fluid from one point to another.

example.text: Disconnect and remove the external hydraulic line at the back of the case.

short: A flat, usually machined surface of a part, especially one that seals against another part.

example.text: A gouged sealing face is a guaranteed leak and may mean a new cover.

short: Any bolt, nut, screw or clip that holds parts together.

example.text: Mark the converter-to-flexplate position, turn the engine to reach each fastener, and remove the converter nuts; discard them.

short: The Subaru 2.5 liter DOHC boxer four in the 2014 to 2018 Forester, one of the units in this app.

example.text: On the FB the camshafts are captured in the carrier; the carrier and cams come off as one unit.

short: Fiat Chrysler Automobiles, the company that owned Chrysler until it became part of Stellantis in 2021.

example.text: FCA issued a bulletin on the C-clutch snap ring in early 948TE units, and a half-seated ring here can destroy the transmission.

short: A set of thin steel blades of exact thicknesses, slid into a gap to measure it.

example.text: Square each new ring in its bore and check the end gap with feeler gauges.

short: The plug removed to add fluid to a transmission.

example.text: With the engine idling, remove the filler plug, add fluid until it just reaches the bottom of the hole, then refit the plug with a new gasket.

short: A small fine mesh set into an oil passage to protect one part from debris.

example.text: The screens are one-time use and protect the oil supply to the AVCS sprockets.

short: The last gear reduction before the wheels, usually built together with the differential.

example.text: On this unit the final drive has its own gear oil, so it is drained and judged on its own.

short: Turned in by hand only, with no tool, so a part can still be moved into line.

example.text: Fit the HP lines finger tight, tighten the unions in sequence, wait 30 seconds and recheck, then paint-mark each line.

short: The order in which the cylinders fire, such as 1-3-2-4.
A flat rim or collar on a part that it bolts or seals against.

example.text: Prying the lower pan off with a screwdriver bends the flange and gouges the sealing face.

short: A tool that holds a sprocket’s flange still while its bolt is turned.

example.text: Hold the oil pump sprocket with the flange holding tool, remove and discard its bolt, and take off the drive chain and sprocket.

short: Engine speed rising briefly during a shift because one clutch let go before the next one gripped.

example.text: Drive and check engagements, smooth ratio change, lock-up, no flare or judder from a stop, and no binding on tight turns.

short: Flat faces ground on a round shaft or hub so a mating part can grip it and turn it.

example.text: Slide the converter on while turning it until it drops through each engagement and the hub's flats engage the pump drive gear.

short: Any liquid; in this app it usually means the oil-like liquid inside a transmission.

example.text: The drained fluid is your first look inside; debris here is what usually condemns the chain and pulleys.

short: A gauge that shows how hard it is pushing, used to put a set load on a clutch pack while its clearance is measured.
The clutch that locks a planetary gear set so it turns as one piece for forward drive.

example.text: On the TR580 the forward clutch rides on the input shaft ahead of the primary pulley.

short: A connecting rod whose cap was cracked off at the factory, so the rough break only fits back on its own rod.

example.text: A fracture-split cap only seats correctly on the rod it was broken from.

short: The height of a spring with no load on it; a spring that has shrunk has lost strength.

example.text: Check each spring's free length, load at installed and open height, and squareness on a surface plate.

short: Dull wear marks from tiny repeated movement between two clamped parts, such as on the back of a bearing shell.
A steel plate faced with friction lining that grips the steel plates beside it when the clutch is applied.

example.text: Stack the C frictions and steels and install the selective snap ring in the case.

short: The cover at the pulley end of the engine that carries the front crank seal.

example.text: Remove the twelve bolts and the front cover, then pull the front crank seal out with the JLR seal tool.

short: A mark or arrow on a part, often on a piston crown, that must face the front of the engine.

example.text: Installing a piston with its crown arrow facing the transmission end.

short: Foot-pound, the US unit of torque; one is about 1.36 N·m.
An electrically opened nozzle that sprays a measured shot of fuel into the engine.

example.text: Remove the four rail bolts and lift the fuel rail away from the injectors.

short: The metal tube that the fuel injectors plug into and that feeds them fuel under pressure.

example.text: Remove the four rail bolts and lift the fuel rail away from the injectors.

short: A threaded plug that closes the end of a drilled oil gallery; removing them lets the galleries be cleaned.

example.text: Remove the water jacket spacers, the oil separator cover, the block plug and main gallery plugs from both halves, and the block plate from the LH half.

short: Damage where two metal surfaces rub under heavy load without enough oil and tear metal from each other.

example.text: Look at all four sheave faces for scoring, steps, galling or bluing where the chain runs.

short: A small space left between two parts, or between the two ends of a split ring.

example.text: Square each ring in its bore with a piston and measure the gap with a feeler gauge.

short: A thin sealing layer clamped between two parts to stop leaks.

example.text: Install the thermostat housing with an undamaged gasket.

short: A solvent that softens old gasket material and sealant so it can be scraped off.

example.text: Remove the O-rings at the heads, the LH block half and the oil pan upper, then strip the old liquid gasket from the cover and engine with gasket remover and plastic scrapers.

short: A toothed wheel that meshes with another to pass turning force from one shaft to another.

example.text: Install the transfer shaft and gears into the rear of the case.

short: A thick oil made for heavily loaded gears, used here in a front differential.

example.text: Fill the front differential with gear oil, not CVTF, and refit its plug.

short: How many turns one shaft makes for each turn of another; a low gear turns the wheels slowly with great force.

example.text: Drive and check engagements, smooth ratio change, lock-up, no flare or judder from a stop, and no binding on tight turns.

short: All the gears and shafts that carry drive through a transmission.

example.text: Lift the geartrain (annulus, B clutch pack and hub, input shaft) out of the case by the input shaft, never by the hub.

short: A gear oil rating for heavily loaded hypoid gears.
A hard, shiny surface on a friction plate or a belt that has been overheated or polished and no longer grips well.
A size class the factory marks on a part, such as a piston or bearing shell, so matching parts can be paired.

example.text: Read the laser-etched letter strings or data-matrix code on the crankshaft for the main and rod journal grades.

short: Letters or a printed code on a crankshaft or block that give each journal’s size grade, used with a chart to pick bearing shells.

example.text: Use the crank codes and the block or rod references with JLR's selection charts to pick a color- and letter-coded shell for each journal.

short: Machining with an abrasive wheel; on a crankshaft it makes worn journals smaller but round again, to suit undersize bearings.

example.text: If journals or pins are out of size or shape, grind to the size that matches the 0.03, 0.05 or 0.25 mm undersize bearings, or replace the crank.

short: The return path for electric current, usually a wire or strap bolted to bare metal.

example.text: Bleed fuel pressure using the factory procedure, remove the fuel filler cap to vent the tank, then disconnect the battery ground.

short: The Ford-built 2.0 liter turbo petrol four that JLR used before the Ingenium.
One of the long, high-strength bolts that clamp the cylinder head to the block.

example.text: In the same sequence, turn every head bolt 90 degrees, then a further 180 degrees.

short: The gasket between the block and the cylinder head that seals in combustion pressure, coolant and oil.

example.text: Catching and tearing the exposed edge of the new head gasket with the cover.

short: Warming an engine fully and letting it cool again, which settles new seals and shows up any leaks.

example.text: Drain the first oil and replace the filter after the initial heat cycle, checking the filter for metal.

short: A device that moves heat from one liquid or gas to another without letting them mix.
A formed metal cover that protects nearby parts from exhaust heat.

example.text: Install the heat shields, using a new bolt where the procedure calls for one.

short: A small heat exchanger behind the dashboard that warms the cabin with hot coolant.

example.text: The repeated rev, wait and top-up cycles work trapped air out of the engine and heater core; air left behind lets the engine overheat.

short: A gear with teeth cut at an angle, which runs more quietly than one with straight teeth.

example.text: Check the balancer needle bearings, the outer races in the block, the helical gear teeth and the anti-backlash scissor gears.

short: An L-shaped six-sided bar that fits bolts with a hexagon-shaped socket in them.
long: Also called an Allen key.

example.text: Push the RH tensioner lever down, lock the plunger with a 2.5 mm pin or hex key in the stopper hole, then remove the tensioner and its lever.

short: A different Subaru CVT fluid, made for larger CVTs; it is the wrong fluid for the CVT in this app.

example.text: Using High Torque CVTF (meant for TR690 units such as the Forester XT) or a generic CVT fluid.

short: Finishing a bore with fine abrasive stones to its exact size and a crosshatch of fine scratches that holds oil for the piston rings.

example.text: Measuring right after honing reads small because the block is still warm.

short: A casting that surrounds and supports other parts.

example.text: With the housing bolted up, the seals can be driven square against a fully supported bore.

short: High pressure: in this app, the label for the fuel pump and lines that carry fuel at very high pressure.

example.text: With the engine idling, check the HP fuel unions, injector seals, turbo oil lines and coolant joints, and listen for chain rattle at the transmission end.

short: The rigid steel pipes that carry fuel from the high-pressure pump to the fuel rail.
long: Each line may only be tightened a limited number of times, and it is paint-marked after every tightening, so count the marks before reusing it.

example.text: Unbolt and remove both high-pressure fuel lines, and count the paint marks on each before deciding whether it can go back on.

short: The pump that raises fuel to very high pressure for direct injection, driven by a cam lobe through a tappet.

example.text: Check the pressed-on cam lobes, the HP fuel pump lobe and the needle roller bearings for pitting or roughness.

short: The center part of a wheel, gear or drum that fits onto a shaft.

example.text: The seal goes on dry; it seals against the pulley hub.

short: A small oil-filled plunger in the head that takes up valve clearance automatically, so it never needs setting by hand.

example.text: Check each exhaust roller follower for a free, smooth roller and each lash adjuster for wear.

short: Pressure in oil or fluid that is used to move or clamp parts.
long: Anything worked this way is called hydraulic.

example.text: Turning the CVVL unit upside down to look at it, which lets air into the hydraulic circuits.

short: A curved-tooth ring gear and pinion whose shafts are offset, so the teeth slide as well as roll.

example.text: If the hypoid gears, bearings or case were replaced, pinion depth and backlash must be re-set before going further.

short: Inside diameter: the measurement across the inside of a hole, tube or hose.
long: On a part, an ID mark is an identification mark.

example.text: Fit new piston seals, then stack the dished cushion plate with its ID mark facing you, soaked frictions alternating with steels, then the pressure plate.

short: A free-turning pulley or sprocket that guides or tightens a belt or chain but drives nothing.

example.text: Install the second new secondary chain guide between the camshaft sprockets, keeping the chain on the idler.

short: A free-turning pulley that guides the accessory belt.

example.text: Refit each idler pulley to its noted position and fit the accessory belt.

short: On the Ingenium, the sprocket between the two timing chains, turned by one and driving the other.

example.text: Lift the secondary chain off the idler sprocket.

short: The coil sitting on each spark plug that turns battery voltage into the high voltage for the spark.

example.text: Install the spark plugs and the four ignition coils.

short: When the spark fires, compared with the piston reaching TDC.
The bladed wheel inside a pump that flings liquid outward to move it.

example.text: Spin the water pump bearing, check the impeller, test the thermostat in heated water, and check the crank pulley, chain cover and pans for cracks.

short: Hardened only at the surface, by heating it with an electric coil and quenching it, so a journal or similar surface resists wear.

example.text: Measure every main and rod journal with a micrometer for size, taper and out-of-round, and check the induction-hardened surfaces for scoring.

short: JLR’s own family of three- and four-cylinder engines, built in the UK and introduced in 2015.
The thin Teflon ring on a direct injector’s tip that seals in combustion pressure; it is fitted and sized with special tools.

example.text: An unsized Teflon seal will not enter the bore cleanly or seal combustion pressure.

short: An engine with four cylinders standing in one straight row.
The shaft that carries drive into the transmission from the torque converter.

example.text: The stopper keeps the converter seated on the transmission input shaft as the engine pulls away.

short: The air-in side of an engine: the parts that carry air into the cylinders.

example.text: Take out the air intake duct and boot, the rear air cleaner case and the radiator.

short: The mushroom-shaped valves in the cylinder head that let air into each cylinder and burned gas out, then seal it shut.

example.text: Turning a cam past its free range to reach a lobe makes intake and exhaust valves collide.

short: The set of passages that carries air from the throttle to each cylinder’s intake port.

example.text: Fit four new port seals and the manifold, then tighten the seven bolts in sequence.

short: An engine in which an open valve and a rising piston can reach the same space, so they collide if the timing slips.

example.text: A timing-tool maker recommends a compression check before the head comes off on this interference engine; it tells you whether valves were already hit.

short: The opposite of a clearance: a part slightly bigger than its hole, pressed or shrunk in and held tight by friction.

example.text: JLR offers one piston size and interference-fit liners, so there is no factory oversize route.

short: A lifting device; the transmission type has a cradle that holds a transmission while it is raised or lowered.

example.text: Hang the engine from a hoist with chains or wire rope and put a jack under the transmission.

short: The British maker of the Land Rover Discovery Sport in this app.
long: Short for Jaguar Land Rover.

example.text: This gasket is a known JLR leak point that causes low fluid, noise and poor shifts.

short: The large bolts that clamp a split block’s two halves, and the main bearings between them, together.

example.text: Lay Plastigage on each journal, join the block halves with oiled bolts and run the full joining-bolt torque sequence, then split the halves and read each strip.

short: The smooth, round part of a shaft that turns inside a bearing.

example.text: Firing a fresh engine before oil pressure is up runs the bearings and cam journals dry.

short: A small metal piece that sits in matching slots in a shaft and a part, locking the part in one position on the shaft.

example.text: Slide the crank sprocket onto the crank key; either face can go outward.

short: Pressing the accelerator to the floor so the transmission drops one or more gears.

example.text: Drive through every upshift to ninth and every downshift, including part-throttle and kickdown shifts, and check the engagements from Park to Reverse to Drive.

short: Part of the fuel and air igniting on its own before the flame reaches it, making a pinging sound that can damage pistons.
A small vibration sensor bolted to the block that hears knock, so the ignition timing can be pulled back.

example.text: Knock sensor orientation affects signal quality; the procedure has you refit them where they came from.

short: Slots or tabs punched in a drum that act as a reluctor ring, so a sensor can read the drum’s speed.

example.text: The drum carries the knockouts that the input speed sensor reads, and bent knockout tabs give a bad speed signal.

short: Kilopascal, a metric unit of pressure; 100 of them make about 14.5 psi.
Turning a valve back and forth on its seat with fine abrasive paste so the two surfaces match and seal.

example.text: Any replaced valve or reworked seat must be lapped so the dye check shows a continuous band.

short: The fine abrasive paste used for lapping; every trace must be cleaned off afterward.

example.text: Leaving lapping compound in a guide or port wears the new guide in minutes.

short: A wooden stick with a suction cup that grips a valve so it can be turned back and forth on its seat.
Left-hand: the left side of the engine or car, as seen from the driver’s seat.

example.text: Install the stud bolts in both heads and the chain cover bolt in the LH head.

short: ZF’s own fluid for its nine-speed automatic.

example.text: Fill through the fill port with ZF LifeguardFluid 9 (JLR part LR023288) to an initial level; do not mix in other fluids or leak dye.

short: The largest or smallest measurement the maker allows before a part must be machined or replaced.

example.text: If guide wear is out of limits, plan on a replacement head.

short: A protective mode where a control module cuts power or holds one gear after it detects a fault.

example.text: Starting the engine and skipping the calibration, which leaves the engine misfiring or in limp mode.

short: Machining a row of bearing bores in one pass so they line up exactly; parts machined together are replaced together.

example.text: If clearance is out, the caps and carrier are replaced as a set because they are line-bored together.

short: The main regulated fluid pressure in an automatic transmission, which feeds every other circuit.

example.text: Worn plunger sleeves let dog clutch pressure overlap or exhaust early; a worn SV-SP feed valve upsets line pressure.

short: Subaru’s brand name for its chain-belt CVTs.
A raised edge, such as the flexible edge of a seal that rides on the shaft, or the tab that locates a bearing shell.

example.text: Pushing the seal over the crank flange without its spacer and rolling the lip.

short: A seal with a flexible rubber edge that a small spring holds against a turning shaft to keep oil in.
Subaru’s name for a sealant paste laid as a bead instead of a cut gasket; it cures into a flexible seal.
long: It starts curing as soon as it is laid, so the parts must be joined within the time the procedure gives, often five minutes. Too thick a bead squeezes into oil passages.

example.text: Run a bead of liquid gasket on a new oil separator cover, fit it to the RH half within five minutes and tighten the bolts in sequence.

short: A spring-loaded pin inside a cam phaser that locks it in its starting position when oil pressure is low.

example.text: If an AVCS lock pin did not engage at shutdown, the sensor plate marks are meaningless and only the housing marks can be trusted.

short: A clutch inside the torque converter that locks it solid at cruising speed, so no power is lost to slip.

example.text: Subaru sells the valve body only as an assembly; the updated design fixes lock-up and shudder faults.

short: A short block with the heads and valvetrain fitted, but without the external parts.
A specialist shop with the machines to resize, straighten and resurface engine parts.
A bearing in the block that one of the crankshaft’s main journals turns in.

example.text: Install the oiled main bearings in both halves in their original or selected positions and fit new O-rings to the LH half.

short: A heavy cap that bolts over a main bearing to hold the crankshaft in the block.

example.text: Tighten the ten main cap bolts in stages to the JLR value and angle, working from the center out.

short: A journal on the crankshaft’s center line, where it turns in the block.

example.text: Oil the main journals and lower the crankshaft into the LH half.

short: The shaft and levers inside the transmission that the selector cable turns.

example.text: Install the parking rod, the manual shaft linkage and a new roll pin in the shift rail.

short: The valve in the valve body that the selector moves directly, routing fluid for park, reverse, neutral and drive.

example.text: A misaligned manual valve leaves the selector and valve body out of step.

short: Manifold absolute pressure sensor: it reports the air pressure inside the intake manifold.

example.text: Loosen the captive bolts, lift off the plastic intake manifold with its throttle and manifold pressure (MAP) sensor, and discard the four port seals.

short: A colored paste spread on a valve face to show where it touches the seat.
A valve body and TCM built into one unit inside the transmission.
M plus a number gives a metric bolt’s thread size in millimeters: an M12 bolt is 12 mm across its threads.

example.text: Clean all threads, including the drive plate holes with an M10 x 1.0 bottoming tap no deeper than the hole, then wash the block and head and blow them dry.

short: A precision screw gauge that measures outside sizes, such as a shaft’s diameter, to a hundredth of a millimeter or finer.

example.text: Measure every main and rod journal with a micrometer for size, taper and out-of-round, and check the induction-hardened surfaces for scoring.

short: Halfway between the top and bottom of a piston’s travel.
The maker of dealer special tools for Chrysler and FCA vehicles.
long: Full name: Miller Special Tools.

short: A cylinder failing to burn its fuel properly, felt as a stumble or shake.

example.text: Starting the engine and skipping the calibration, which leaves the engine misfiring or in limp mode.

short: The year a maker assigns to a vehicle version, written with MY after it; it can differ from the year it was built.
A gasket made of several thin, embossed steel layers; it needs very flat, clean, dry faces to seal.

example.text: Fit the two clean dowels to the block and lay a new multi-layer steel gasket over them.

short: Newton-meter, the metric unit of torque used for most tightening values in this app.
A rolling bearing with many long, thin rollers, so it fits in very little space.

example.text: Check the pressed-on cam lobes, the HP fuel pump lobe and the needle roller bearings for pitting or roughness.

short: The standard design size given in the spec, before any wear or machining.
Noise, vibration and harshness: how loud and rough a car feels.
long: NVH pads are foam blocks fitted around the engine to make it quieter.

example.text: Unclip and remove the foam and laminate NVH (noise, vibration and harshness) pads from the block sides, head and timing cover area.

short: A rubber ring with a round cross-section that seals by being squeezed in a groove.

example.text: Fit the speed sensors and the secondary pressure sensor with new O-rings.

short: A deep socket with a slot for an oxygen sensor’s wire; in this app it is used as a pushing tool.
Not on the same center line as the input shaft; a pump mounted this way is driven by a chain.
The unit of electrical resistance.
long: Its symbol is Ω.

short: A meter that measures electrical resistance in ohms.

example.text: Power the dog clutch pressure sensor from a bench supply and apply air to confirm its output changes; an ohmmeter will not test it.

short: A slippery liquid that keeps moving metal parts from touching and carries heat away.

example.text: The first oil carries assembly lube and machining debris.

short: The gap between a bearing and its journal, which fills with the film of oil the shaft rides on.
long: Too little, and the bearing can run dry and fail; too much, and the oil escapes too fast to hold the shaft up.

example.text: Main clearance can only be read with the two halves clamped exactly as they will run.

short: How much oil an engine burns or loses between oil changes.

example.text: Installing the second ring upside down raises oil consumption.

short: A solenoid valve that steers engine oil on command, for example to move a cam phaser.

example.text: Fit the oil control solenoids with new oiled O-rings, plus the sensor and actuator covers.

short: A small heat exchanger that passes engine oil close to coolant to take heat out of the oil.

example.text: Fit a new metal gasket and the oil cooler, and tighten the seven bolts in sequence in two stages.

short: The thin layer of oil, under pressure, that keeps a journal floating off its bearing.

example.text: This is the only check of the actual oil film the rod bearing will run on.

short: A paper element in a housing that catches dirt and metal particles before the oil reaches the bearings.

example.text: Open the filler cap, drain the oil from the pan, refit the drain plug with a new gasket and spin off the oil filter.

short: A drilled passage in the block or head that carries oil from the pump to the parts that need it.

example.text: Measuring dirty parts gives false readings, and a blocked gallery starves a bearing.

short: A bolted plate that closes oil passages in the transmission case; its gasket is a known leak point.

example.text: Fit the oil gallery plate with a new bonded gasket and new bolts, and tighten the bolts in sequence.

short: The tray bolted under an engine or transmission that holds its oil or fluid.

example.text: Unbolt and lift off the oil pan, then look at the magnet and the bottom of the pan for chain or pulley debris.

short: A thin blade driven into a sealed joint to cut the sealant, so the flange does not have to be pried.

example.text: Unbolt the oil pan upper and lift it off together with the lower pan, then take the O-ring off the block; if the lower pan must be separated, cut its sealant with an oil pan cutter.

short: A rigid cast upper section of the oil pan that bolts to the block and carries other parts.

example.text: Connect the water pipe hoses at the oil pan upper and bolt the water pipe assemblies on.

short: The pipe that dips into the oil pan and feeds the pump, with a mesh cover on its end to keep out large debris.

example.text: Bolt the pan baffle back on, then install a new oil strainer with a new O-ring.

short: The pressure the oil pump builds in the galleries, which keeps the bearings floating on oil.

example.text: Firing a fresh engine before oil pressure is up runs the bearings and cam journals dry.

short: A switch that turns on the dashboard warning light when oil pressure is too low.

example.text: Start the engine and confirm oil pressure with a gauge in place of the pressure switch, then look for leaks and listen for noise.

short: The pump that pushes oil under pressure to the bearings and other moving parts.

example.text: Hold the oil pump sprocket with the flange holding tool, remove and discard its bolt, and take off the drive chain and sprocket.

short: The bottom piston ring, made of two thin rails and a wavy expander, that scrapes oil off the cylinder wall.

example.text: Install the oil control ring, then the two compression rings, and turn them so the gaps are 120 degrees apart.

short: A box or cover with baffles that strips oil mist out of the crankcase gas before it goes to the intake.

example.text: Loosen the captive bolts and lift off the engine vent oil separator, discarding its gasket.

short: A part running with too little oil, which wears it fast or makes it seize.

example.text: A turbo that failed from oil starvation or contamination will fail again on a fresh engine.

short: A rating such as 10W-40: the first number shows how easily the oil flows cold, the second how thick it stays hot.

example.text: Fill with 0W-20 synthetic oil through the filler to the F mark on the dipstick.

short: A label for parts, such as many fasteners and seals, that must be replaced with new ones whenever they are removed.
long: Makers word it differently: one-time use, single use and renew all mean fit a new part.

example.text: Subaru lists this ring as one-time use.

short: A block design where the coolant passage around the cylinder tops is open at the deck, with no bracing to the outer wall.
A small, precise hole that limits how fast fluid can flow through a passage.

example.text: Setting the support down a tooth off so the tube orifices do not line up.

short: Wear that leaves a bore or journal slightly oval instead of truly round.

example.text: Measure each bore for taper and out-of-round, measure each piston skirt, and compare the two.

short: The gear at the end of the gear train that passes drive on to the transfer gear.

example.text: Install the transfer gear on its bearing meshed with the output gear, then the differential meshed with the transfer pinion.

short: Taking a unit fully apart, renewing worn parts and rebuilding it to factory condition.

example.text: JLR dealers replace the whole transmission for internal faults; an overhaul only makes sense when parts, tooling and service data are in hand.

short: Made larger than standard, such as pistons for a cylinder that has been machined bigger.

example.text: JLR lists only one piston diameter grade, so a worn bore cannot be fixed with a factory oversize piston.

short: The free gap in a released clutch pack; too loose and it slips, too tight and it drags.

example.text: Measure pack clearance with a feeler gauge and change the selective plate until it is in range.

short: A dab of paint on a fitting or bolt that records a tightening, so later turns or reuses can be checked.

example.text: JLR allows each HP line a limited number of tightening cycles and has you paint-mark it after each one.

short: The toothed gear on the output that the parking pawl locks.

example.text: Remove the transfer gear (with its integral park gear) from its bearing.

short: A hinged steel catch with a tooth that drops into a gear in park so the car cannot roll.

example.text: Take out the parking pawl with its spring and pivot shaft.

short: The rod, with a wedge on its end, that the selector pushes to force the parking pawl into its gear.

example.text: Pull the parking rod out before the case is touched.

short: JLR’s current dealer diagnostic software, used on newer vehicles.
The control module that runs the engine: it reads the sensors and controls fuel and spark.
long: Short for powertrain control module.

example.text: With the engine still in the vehicle, scan the engine computer (PCM) and save every stored code and the camshaft timing data.

short: The system that draws crankcase gas into the intake to be burned; its one-way valve meters the flow.
long: Short for positive crankcase ventilation.

example.text: Coat the PCV valve threads with liquid gasket, install it in the RH half and refit its hose.

short: A bolt fitted and tightened first to pull a part into its correct position before the rest go in.

example.text: Fit the coolant pump, tighten the two locating bolts first, then the other four, and fit the pulley.

short: A short rod used to locate, hold or hinge parts.

example.text: Once the pin is out the chain is loaded and cannot be shifted a tooth without starting over.

short: The pins that fit a pulley wrench to the holes in a particular pulley or sprocket.

example.text: Hold the water pump pulley with the pulley wrench and pin set and remove its bolts.

short: The clearance between a piston pin and the small-end bushing it turns in.

example.text: Where pin-to-bushing clearance is out, press out the bushing, press in a new oiled one, drill its two oil holes through the rod's holes and ream it to fit.

short: The smaller of two meshing gears, or any small gear that drives a bigger one.

example.text: Spin each planetary pinion for roughness and end play, and check every needle thrust bearing and washer.

short: How far the drive pinion reaches into the ring gear, set with shims so the teeth mesh in the right spot.

example.text: If the hypoid gears, bearings or case were replaced, pinion depth and backlash must be re-set before going further.

short: The housing that holds the drive pinion and its bearings.

example.text: Remove the pinion support bolts and pry the support up with the drive pinion, saving the two seals.

short: A close-fitting plug that slides in a cylinder; pressure on one side pushes it along.
long: In the engine, burning fuel pushes each piston down to turn the main shaft. In a transmission, fluid pressure pushes a piston to squeeze a stack of plates together.

example.text: Turning the crank counterclockwise here can bring a piston up into an open valve.

short: A small nozzle in the bottom of the block that sprays oil up under a piston to cool it.

example.text: Bolt the four piston cooling jets back into the block and check that each one points at the underside of its piston.

short: The top face of a piston, which takes the force of combustion.

example.text: Confirm each rod and cap is marked to its cylinder and note the arrow on each piston crown toward the front.

short: The hardened steel tube through the piston and the rod’s small end that lets the rod pivot.
long: Also called a gudgeon pin.

example.text: Join each piston to its rod with the piston pin and two new circlips, keeping the crown arrow and rod orientation correct.

short: Plugged access holes in older Subaru boxer blocks for reaching the piston pins with the block still assembled; newer Subaru engines have none.

example.text: The FB has no piston pin service holes; its diagonally split rods let the piston and rod leave through the bore once the head is off.

short: A thin split metal ring in a groove around the piston that seals against the cylinder wall.
The lower sides of a piston, which keep it upright in the cylinder.

example.text: Staggered gaps limit blow-by, and no gap may sit in line with the piston skirt.

short: The clearance between a piston and its cylinder wall, found by subtracting the piston size from the bore size.
Small craters in a hard surface, such as a gear tooth or bearing, where metal has flaked away from fatigue or corrosion.

example.text: Check the pressed-on cam lobes, the HP fuel pump lobe and the needle roller bearings for pitting or roughness.

short: The frame that holds the small orbiting gears of a gear set on their pins.

example.text: Install the planet carrier and ring gear, turning them until the splines drop in.

short: One of several small gears, held on a carrier, that circle around a center gear.

example.text: Check the planet pinions for play and pitting, and the ring and sun gear teeth and oil slots.

short: A sun gear, planet gears on a planet carrier, and a ring gear; holding one part while driving another gives a new ratio.

example.text: Separate the input shaft and B clutch drum from the shared housing of planetary sets 3 and 4.

short: A soft-faced hammer that taps parts free without denting them.

example.text: Tap the RH head loose with a plastic hammer, remove the last two bolts and lift the head and gasket off without scratching either face.

short: A scraper that removes old gasket and sealant without gouging soft aluminum faces.

example.text: Remove the old gasket and RTV from the aluminum head, block and cover faces with a plastic scraper and solvent only.

short: A brand of soft plastic thread laid across a journal; the clamped bearing flattens it, and its width shows the oil clearance.
long: The width is read against a printed scale on the packet. The shaft must not be turned while the strip is in place, or it smears and reads wrong.

example.text: Turning the crank with Plastigage in place smears it and gives a false reading.

short: A flat piece of metal, such as a cover, a spacer or one disc in a stack.

example.text: Lifting by the hub pulls it out of the B clutch pack and drops the plates.

short: Free movement between two parts that are meant to fit together closely.

example.text: Check the planet pinions for play and pitting, and the ring and sun gear teeth and oil slots.

short: A sliding rod or small piston, moved by a spring or by fluid pressure.

example.text: The plunger is spring and oil loaded; pinning it first keeps it from shooting out and lets it be reused.

short: A valve in the valve body that feeds oil to a dog clutch; worn sleeves around these valves cause dog clutch faults.

example.text: Check the pressure regulator, the valve that feeds it (the SV-SP valve) and the A/F dog plunger valve sleeves for bore wear and sticking.

short: An opening where a passage for gas or fluid starts or ends, such as the duct in a head that leads to a valve.

example.text: Doubling up old and new port O-rings, which holds the valve body off the case.

short: Spraying fuel into each intake port, just upstream of the intake valve.
A rubber seal between the intake manifold and the head at each port.

example.text: Fit four new port seals and the manifold, then tighten the seven bolts in sequence.

short: The engine and transmission together: the parts that make the drive and pass it on.

example.text: Mate the engine to the ZF 9HP48 transmission and refit the powertrain to the vehicle following the vehicle procedures.

short: A bolt with a factory patch of thread-locking compound that only works once.
A load deliberately built in during assembly, such as clamping bearings tight or compressing a spring before it does any work.

example.text: These shims set transfer gear bearing preload and end play; reusing them in the right place saves a full measurement.

short: How hard a gas or liquid pushes on every part of the surface around it.

example.text: An unsized Teflon seal will not enter the bore cleanly or seal combustion pressure.

short: The thick end plate that a clutch pack is squeezed against.

example.text: With a resealed piston, lay in the apply plate, then alternate steel and friction four times, then the pressure plate and snap ring.

short: A valve that holds line pressure at the level the TCM asks for.

example.text: Check the pressure regulator, the valve that feeds it (the SV-SP valve) and the A/F dog plunger valve sleeves for bore wear and sticking.

short: A sensor that reports the fluid pressure in a hydraulic circuit.

example.text: Remove the speed sensors and the secondary pressure sensor and cap the bores.

short: The Ingenium’s lower timing chain, from the crankshaft to the idler sprocket.

example.text: Remove the idler sprocket bolt, lift off the idler sprocket and slip the primary chain off the crankshaft sprocket.

short: The input pulley of a CVT, turned by the engine.

example.text: Remove the bolts that retain the primary pulley on the right side.

short: Filling a system or part with oil before the first start, so nothing runs dry.
