example.text: Pre-oiling the bearings protects them during the seconds before oil pressure reaches the turbo on first crank.

short: The long shaft under the car that carries drive to the rear axle.

example.text: Refit the crossmember, axles with new C-clips, propeller shaft, cooler lines and harness, flushing the cooler circuit first.

short: Standing slightly above the surface around it.

example.text: Lower the geartrain by the input shaft and wriggle it until it engages both packs with a solid clunk and the D hub sits just proud of the pack.

short: A flat steel bar for levering parts apart, used only at the points the maker provides.

example.text: Ease the valve body away from the connecting tubes with a suitable pry tool, keeping its harness to the range and speed sensors slack.

short: Metric horsepower, slightly smaller than US horsepower: 240 of them is about 237 hp.
Pounds per square inch, the US unit of pressure.
JLR’s code for the 2.0 liter Ingenium turbo petrol inline four in this app.
A small gearbox on the side of a front-drive transmission that turns drive toward the rear wheels.
long: Short for power transfer unit.

example.text: Refit the PTU to the differential side with a new seal, then refit the halfshafts, cooler lines, harness and selector.

short: A grooved wheel on a shaft that a belt or chain runs around.

example.text: Bolt the water pump pulley on while holding it with the pulley wrench.

short: A tool that forces a CVT secondary pulley open against its spring so the chain goes slack.

example.text: Fit the pulley expander tool and tighten it evenly on both sides until the secondary pulley opens and the chain goes slack.

short: A Subaru special wrench that holds a pulley or sprocket still while its bolt is turned.

example.text: Hold the water pump pulley with the pulley wrench and pin set and remove its bolts.

short: A device that moves a liquid or gas, usually pushing it out under pressure.

example.text: The pump is chain-driven from the converter at about 1.33 times engine speed.

short: A short chain that turns a pump mounted off to one side.

example.text: Lift off the oil pump drive chain and its sprockets together.

short: A valve that lets stored fuel vapor be drawn into the intake to be burned.

example.text: Disconnect the breather pipe connectors and remove the breather pipe, then unbolt the evaporative purge valve assembly.

short: US quart, a liquid measure a little under one liter.
A push-on fitting for fuel and other hoses that is released with a small tool instead of unscrewed.

example.text: Unplug each injector, disconnect the fuel pipe quick connectors and unbolt each fuel pipe from its cam carrier with its injectors.

short: One of the hardened rings that the balls or rollers of a rolling bearing run on.

example.text: Pressing on the outer race brinells a new bearing.

short: Play across a shaft, from side to side.

example.text: Check the turbo shaft for radial and axial play, wheel contact and coked oil in the center housing, and confirm the oil feed and return pipes are clear.

short: The finned heat exchanger at the front of the car that cools the coolant with passing air.

example.text: The radiator sits directly in front of the crank pulley and must be out of the way for the engine to roll forward.

short: A sensor on the manual shaft that reports which selector position is chosen.
long: Subaru calls it the inhibitor switch.

example.text: Bolt the inhibitor switch on loosely, set it to the neutral position and tighten it.

short: A fluted cutting tool turned through a hole, such as a bushing, to bring it to an exact finished size.

example.text: Where pin-to-bushing clearance is out, press out the bushing, press in a new oiled one, drill its two oil holes through the rod's holes and ream it to fit.

short: A boxed set of the gaskets, seals and other wear parts a rebuild needs.

example.text: A typical aftermarket rebuild kit leaves out the oil pump and timing parts, so chains, guides or tensioners must be sourced separately if needed.

short: A machine that pumps refrigerant out of an A/C system and stores it.

example.text: Have the A/C system evacuated with a recovery machine before any refrigerant line is opened.

short: The gas that carries heat in the air conditioning system; it must be recovered by machine, never vented.

example.text: The compressor leaves with the engine, so its hoses must be disconnected, and refrigerant may not be vented.

short: Clearing a module’s old learned values and running a procedure so it learns the new parts.
long: Subaru calls this AT learning.

example.text: The TCM must relearn clutch and pressure characteristics of the rebuilt parts.

short: A spring-loaded valve that opens to cap the highest pressure a pump can make.
A toothed ring or plate that a speed or position sensor reads as the teeth pass it.

example.text: Timing to a free-floating sensor plate instead of the housing marks puts the cam out of time.

short: A used unit overhauled to factory standards, usually by a specialist, and sold as an exchange.

example.text: Decide whether the converter can be reused or should go to a converter rebuilder or be replaced with a remanufactured unit.

short: How strongly a wire or coil holds back the flow of electric current.
Machining a warped face flat again by taking off a very thin layer of metal.

example.text: Have the decks resurfaced only if they are past the warpage limit, and never below the minimum block height.

short: A part that holds another in place, most often the cap that holds a valve spring on its valve.

example.text: Compress the E Belleville spring, remove its retainer, then lift the bonded piston out of the steel drum.

short: A spring that pushes a clutch piston back when pressure is released.

example.text: Check all three packs: frictions for burning and lost material, steels for heat spots and warping, and pistons, seals, return springs and drum bores for scoring.

short: A brake that holds part of a planetary gear set so the output turns backward.

example.text: Remove the housing support bolts, then lift out the reverse brake plates in order, noting which way the dished cushion plate faces.

short: Right-hand: the right side of the engine or car, as seen from the driver’s seat.
long: Subaru labels many parts by the side they sit on, and the right and left versions are not interchangeable.

example.text: Fit the EGR pipe to the water pipe and RH block half with a new gasket.

short: A band that squeezes the piston rings into their grooves so the piston can be tapped into its cylinder.

example.text: Fit each piston with its graded rod shell, arrow toward the front, and tap it into the bore through a ring compressor while guiding the rod onto the journal.

short: The gap between the two ends of a piston ring when it is squared in its cylinder.
long: Too small, and the ends butt together as the ring heats up, which can break the ring or scuff the cylinder. Too large, and more combustion gas leaks past.

example.text: Square each new ring in its bore and check the end gap with feeler gauges.

short: Pliers that open a piston ring just enough to slide it over the piston without bending it.

example.text: Fit the oil ring expander, lower rail and upper rail by hand, then the second and top rings with a ring expander, marks facing up.

short: Turning each piston ring so its gap sits away from the others, which limits blow-by.

example.text: Staggered gaps limit blow-by, and no gap may sit in line with the piston skirt.

short: A gear shaped like a ring, with teeth around its inside or outside edge.

example.text: The balancers are gear-driven from a ring gear on the crankshaft, so the crank must come out first.

short: One of the grooves around a piston that a ring sits in.

example.text: Clean the ring grooves, roll each compression ring in its groove and measure the side clearance with a feeler gauge.

short: A scraper that cleans carbon out of piston ring grooves.
The raised band of metal between the grooves that sealing rings sit in.

example.text: Check the bushings, the sealing ring grooves, the steel sealing-ring support pressed into the case and the ring lands on the stator support.

short: The cover on top of the head over the camshafts.
long: Also called a valve cover.

example.text: The rocker covers go on before the chain cover because the chain cover seals across their ends.

short: The post that one end of a roller rocker rocks on.

example.text: Lift out the RH roller rockers, O-rings, valve shims and rocker pivots and store each in a labeled tray by valve.

short: A gauge stand that checks whether a connecting rod is bent or twisted.

example.text: Check each rod for bend and twist on a rod aligner and look over the thrust faces and small-end bushing.

short: The bearing inside a connecting rod’s big end that turns on its crank pin.

example.text: This is the only check of the actual oil film the rod bearing will run on.

short: One of the high-strength bolts that clamp a rod cap to its rod.

example.text: Rod bolts are stretch-type and one-time use; the angle sets clamp load, not the torque reading.

short: A thin special socket that reaches the Subaru rod bolts.
The removable lower half of a connecting rod’s big end.

example.text: Mixing rod caps between rods ruins the bore geometry; each cap only fits its own rod.

short: A split spring-steel tube driven into a hole to locate or lock two parts together.

example.text: Install the parking rod, the manual shaft linkage and a new roll pin in the shift rail.

short: A short lever with a roller that rides under a cam lobe; one end rests on a lash adjuster, the other pushes the valve.

example.text: Check each exhaust roller follower for a free, smooth roller and each lash adjuster for wear.

short: A pivoting arm with a small roller that the cam lobe pushes; the arm in turn pushes the valve open.

example.text: Setting the carrier with a lobe on a rocker can bend a valve or crack the carrier.

short: A bearing in which balls or rollers roll between an inner and an outer ring.

example.text: Unbolt and separate the pump halves, check the gears, body, shaft and shaft bearings for wear and pitting, and check the pump drive chain and sprockets.

short: The turning part inside a pump or similar unit.

example.text: Check the vane pump faces, vanes and rotor, check the drive chain for stretch, and inspect the four flats on the pump drive gear where the converter hub engages.

short: Revolutions per minute: how many full turns a shaft makes each minute.

example.text: For the first 1,000 miles keep the engine under 4,000 rpm, vary speed, avoid hard starts and hard braking, and check the oil level often.

short: A sealant that cures by reacting with moisture in the air.
long: Short for room-temperature vulcanizing silicone. It does the same job as liquid gasket. Parts must be fitted and tightened before it skins over, which is why the steps give a time limit such as 7 minutes.

example.text: Letting the RTV skin over before the pan is torqued.

short: One of the passages in an intake manifold that leads to a single cylinder.
A change a maker makes partway through production, without waiting for a new model year.
How much a turning shaft or surface wobbles away from true, read on a dial indicator as it is turned.

example.text: Crack-check the crank, check runout on the end journals with a dial gauge, and mic every main journal and crank pin for size, taper and out-of-round.

short: A tool that plugs into the car to read trouble codes and live data and to run service routines.

example.text: Idle the engine and watch the CVTF temperature on the scan tool until it reaches the check window.

short: A gear made of two spring-loaded halves that grip the meshing teeth from both sides, taking out backlash and rattle.

example.text: Check the balancer needle bearings, the outer races in the block, the helical gear teeth and the anti-backlash scissor gears.

short: Scratches or grooves cut into a surface by dirt or metal particles, or by parts running short of oil.

example.text: Look at all four sheave faces for scoring, steps, galling or bluing where the chain runs.

short: Rubbing marks on a sliding surface, such as a piston skirt, from metal touching metal without enough oil.
Symptom Driven Diagnostics, JLR’s older dealer diagnostic software.
A part that stops oil, fluid, gas or dirt from passing through a joint.

example.text: A seal driven too deep blocks the oil passage beside it.

short: A smooth sleeve that slides a new lip seal over a shaft without folding its lip.

example.text: Oil the new rear seal inside and out and press it on with the seal guide and installer.

short: A driver shaped to press a seal in squarely to the right depth.

example.text: Drive new differential seals into the case and bell housing with the seal installer.

short: A paste or liquid that fills a joint and hardens to seal it.

example.text: The head must go on within five minutes of applying sealant.

short: A narrow plastic or iron ring in a groove on a shaft that seals fluid passing between a fixed part and a turning one.

example.text: Fit new sealing rings on the pulley shafts and input shaft and lubricate them with CVTF.

short: A soft metal or rubber-faced washer that seals a bolt or fitting as it is tightened.

example.text: Unbolt the support bracket, then remove the turbo oil feed pipe, cutting off the trapped lower sealing washers and discarding both banjo bolts and all four washers.

short: The surface that a part rests or seals on.

example.text: Any replaced valve or reworked seat must be lapped so the dye check shows a continuous band.

short: Machining a valve seat with angled cutters, centered by the valve guide, to restore its shape and contact band.

example.text: Guides go in before seat work because the seat cutter pilots off the guide bore.

short: The lower compression ring, which also scrapes oil and must be fitted with its mark facing up.

example.text: Installing the second ring upside down raises oil consumption.

short: The Ingenium’s upper timing chain, from the idler sprocket to the camshafts.

example.text: Lift the secondary chain off the idler sprocket.

short: The output pulley of a CVT, driven from the primary pulley; a strong spring holds it closed.

example.text: The chain cannot come off a loaded pulley, and the secondary pulley is held closed by a strong spring.

short: To jam or weld together because the oil film failed or the clearance was too small.

example.text: Too much sealant here can flow onto a journal and seize the camshaft.

short: A clutch plate made in several thicknesses; choosing the right one sets the pack clearance.

example.text: Measure pack clearance with a feeler gauge and change the selective plate until it is in range.

short: A snap ring made in several thicknesses; picking the right one sets a clutch pack’s clearance.

example.text: With the specified force on the pack, measure clearance and change the selective snap ring until it is in range.

short: The lever or dial the driver uses to pick park, reverse, neutral or drive.

example.text: Refit the PTU to the differential side with a new seal, then refit the halfshafts, cooler lines, harness and selector.

short: A small valve on the A dog clutch that changes the pressure signal its sensor sees as the dog engages.

example.text: Check that the small screw holding the A dog sensing valve plate is tight and its head is intact.

short: A part that measures something, such as speed, position, pressure or temperature, and reports it as an electrical signal.

example.text: The TCM uses this sensor to know when either dog has finished moving.

short: A thin plate with drilled holes that sits between valve body sections and meters the flow between them.

example.text: Unbolt the manual valve body and separator plate from the reverse brake housing.

short: A plugged opening that lets you reach the bolts between the drive plate and the torque converter.

example.text: Remove the service hole plug, then turn the crank by the pulley bolt to bring each torque converter bolt into reach and remove it.

short: The maker’s repair instructions, with procedures, tightening sequences and specifications.

example.text: No published value could be verified for this engine, so take it from the JLR workshop manual.

short: A long round bar that turns, or that holds parts which turn.

example.text: Fit new sealing rings on the pulley shafts and input shaft and lubricate them with CVTF.

short: One cone-shaped half of a CVT pulley; one half slides in and out to change the pulley’s working size.

example.text: A sudden release lets the spring slam the sheaves onto a misplaced chain.

short: Any clutch, brake or dog clutch that the TCM applies or releases to change gear.
A precision spacer made in graded thicknesses, used to set a clearance, an end play or a part’s position.

example.text: Pulley shims set where each pulley sits; a wrong stack misaligns the chain.

short: The block with its crankshaft, rods and pistons fitted, but no heads.
A shaking vibration when a clutch grabs and slips in quick succession.
long: Also called judder.

example.text: Subaru sells the valve body only as an assembly; the updated design fixes lock-up and shudder faults.

short: Of a piston or sliding sleeve: to slide fully from one end of its travel to the other.

example.text: Apply air to the F dog apply and release ports and confirm the sleeve shuttles fully both ways.

short: Clearance measured across a part’s width, such as a piston ring in its groove or a connecting rod beside its neighbor.

example.text: Clean the ring grooves, roll each compression ring in its groove and measure the side clearance with a feeler gauge.

short: The gears inside a differential: two drive the axles, and small ones between them let the axles turn at different speeds.
Steel made by pressing metal powder in a mold and heating it until the grains bond; used for parts such as bearing caps.

example.text: Loosen the ten main cap bolts evenly and lift out the five numbered sintered-steel caps with their shells.

short: A close-fitting tube: either a lining in a bore for a sliding part to run in, or a sliding collar that locks parts together.

example.text: The sleeve usually wears before the gears; spline damage here causes loss of forward gears.

short: Machining out a damaged cylinder and pressing in a new liner.

example.text: Within limits, hone lightly and fit new rings; with liner scoring or wear beyond limits, replace the block or send it to a specialist for sleeving.

short: A weight sliding on a rod that pulls a stuck part out with sharp blows.

example.text: Discard the injector spring clamps, fit the JLR injector remover with a slide hammer, and pull each centrally mounted injector straight out of the head.

short: Thick, tar-like deposits from broken-down oil that can clog small oil passages.

example.text: Drain a clean sample of the used oil into a bottle and note its smell, color and any sludge before draining the rest.

short: The small top eye of a connecting rod, where it joins the piston.
A small expanding probe set to the size of a hole, then measured with a micrometer.
A pressed-in bronze bushing in a rod’s small end that the piston pin swings in.

example.text: Measure the piston pin and the rod small-end bushing and subtract.

short: A spring-steel ring that snaps into a groove to hold a part on a shaft or in a bore.
long: Some fly off hard when released, so wear eye protection.

example.text: Release the press and confirm the C snap ring is fully seated in its groove all the way around.

short: Tight enough to hold parts firmly together, but short of the final torque.

example.text: Checking mains with only a few bolts snug gives a reading that is too loose.

short: An electric coil that pulls a plunger when powered, used to open, close or meter a valve.

example.text: Measure each solenoid at room temperature, then recheck the lock-up solenoid hot, because it often opens only when warm.

short: A parts washer with a pump and brush that circulates cleaning solvent.
The plug screwed into the head whose spark lights the fuel and air.

example.text: Install the spark plugs, then the four ignition coils.

short: A value the maker sets, such as a torque, a clearance or a fluid type.
long: Short for specification.

example.text: Run the case bolts down and torque them to spec in a crossing pattern.

short: A tool made for one particular job on one design, usually sold through the maker’s dealers.

example.text: These seals are single use and are sized on the injector at refit with special tools.

short: A sensor that reads how fast a shaft or drum in the transmission is turning.

example.text: Check the speed sensors, the range sensor and the connector plate wiring for chafing, heat damage and bad terminals.

short: A short pipe stub on a housing that a hose pushes onto.

example.text: Ignoring seepage at the thermostat housing; JLR has bulletins on coolant leaks from this housing's welded spigot and gasket.

short: Matching ridges and grooves on a shaft and a hub that lock them together in rotation while letting them slide.

example.text: Install the planet carrier and ring gear, turning them until the splines drop in.

short: A sliding valve with raised lands and narrow waists, like a cotton reel, that opens and closes fluid passages as it moves.
A coil or disc of springy steel that pushes back when squeezed and returns to shape.

example.text: Check each spring's free length, load at installed and open height, and squareness on a surface plate.

short: The washer under a valve spring that it sits on.

example.text: Pull and discard every valve stem seal, which also carries the spring seat.

short: A small press with a gauge that shows how much force a spring gives at a set height.
A toothed wheel that a chain wraps around.

example.text: Check the crank sprocket mark is still at the parked position with all pistons halfway down.

short: A special socket for the bolts that hold the cam sprockets.

example.text: Hold each sprocket with the pulley wrench and pin sets (a 6 mm rod through the RH exhaust sprocket), remove the bolts with the sprocket socket and tag each sprocket by position.

short: A bearing shell dragged round in its housing by a seizing shaft, usually damaging the housing too.

example.text: Reusing old rod bolts or skipping the angle lets a cap loosen and spin a bearing.

short: How upright a spring stands on a flat plate; a leaning spring pushes unevenly.

example.text: Check each spring's free length, load at installed and open height, and squareness on a surface plate.

short: Sealant pushed out of a joint as it is clamped; it is wiped off exposed faces.

example.text: Remove the temporary head bolts, install the separate outer joining bolt and wipe any squeeze-out off the chain cover and oil pan faces, leaving sealant on the chamfers.

short: Subaru’s dealer scan tool software.
long: Short for Subaru Select Monitor.

short: The total of all the parts stacked along a shaft, which decides the clearances left over.

example.text: A bearing left on the hub ends up out of position and wrecks the stack-up.

short: Locking a nut by punching part of its collar into a slot in the shaft so it cannot unscrew.

example.text: Forgetting to restake the nut after torquing it.

short: The highest engine speed reached with the accelerator floored and the car held still in gear; it tests the converter.
A system that shuts the engine off when the car stops and restarts it to move off.
The electric motor that turns the engine over to start it.

example.text: Remove the starter, attach the torque converter stopper to the converter housing, then remove the upper transmission-to-engine bolts.

short: The finned wheel in the middle of a torque converter that redirects fluid to multiply torque; it can turn only one way.
The fixed hollow shaft that holds the stator and carries fluid to and from the converter.

example.text: Bolt the stator support to the bell housing with new sealing rings.

short: A plain, unlined metal plate stacked between the lined plates of a clutch.

example.text: Stack the C frictions and steels and install the selective snap ring in the case.

short: The clearance between a valve stem and the guide it slides in, found by subtracting the stem size from the guide bore.
Changing ratio smoothly, with no separate gears to step between.
Jerky tightening where a bolt grabs and then jumps, so the torque reading cannot be trusted.

example.text: If a bolt creaks with stick-slip while tightening, the whole procedure has to be restarted with fresh sealant.

short: Subaru Technical Information System, Subaru’s paid website for service manuals and bulletins.
JLR’s engine oil specification; the oil must be approved to it, not just labeled 0W-20.

example.text: Fill with 0W-20 oil meeting STJLR.51.5122 and check the level on the dipstick.

short: A pin pushed through a tensioner to hold its plunger back until the chain is fitted.

example.text: Recheck the blue and two pink links against their marks, then pull the stopper pin so the tensioner takes up the slack.

short: A precision steel bar laid across a surface; feeler gauges slid under it show how much the surface is warped.

example.text: Check both head faces of the block with a straightedge and feeler gauge.

short: How far a piston travels from the top of its cylinder to the bottom.
A rod threaded at both ends: one end screws into the part and a nut clamps on the other.

example.text: Install the stud bolts in both heads and the chain cover bolt in the LH head.

short: A group of parts built up off the main unit, then installed as one piece.

example.text: Wash every part in clean solvent, blow passages dry with air, and keep each subassembly's parts together.

short: To send part of a job out to a specialist shop instead of doing it yourself.
The center gear of a gear set, which the planet gears circle around.

example.text: Fitted backward, the sun gear cuts off lube oil to the planetary.

short: Subaru’s ready-mixed long-life coolant.

example.text: Add the cooling system conditioner and fill with Subaru Super Coolant.

short: A thick, very flat plate used as a reference surface when checking parts for warpage.

example.text: Check each spring's free length, load at installed and open height, and squareness on a surface plate.

short: A valve in the valve body of the nine-speed; wear in its bore upsets line pressure.

example.text: Worn plunger sleeves let dog clutch pressure overlap or exhaust early; a worn SV-SP feed valve upsets line pressure.

short: Splines with pointed, angled tooth ends that help a dog clutch slide into mesh.

example.text: Check the F dog sleeve and its two sealing rings, and the synchro splines on the sun gear shared by sets 1 and 2.

short: Oil made from chemically built base stocks, which holds up better to heat and flows better cold.

example.text: Fill with 0W-20 synthetic oil through the filler to the F mark on the dipstick.

short: Wear that leaves a bore or journal bigger at one end than the other.

example.text: Measure each bore for taper and out-of-round, measure each piston skirt, and compare the two.

short: A rolling bearing with cone-shaped rollers that takes both side and end loads; it is usually set with preload.

example.text: Check the tapered bearings on the transfer gear and differential, the park gear teeth and pawl, and the park rod and its cam.

short: A sliding cup, often with a roller, that a cam lobe pushes to drive a pump plunger.

example.text: Lift the HP fuel pump tappet out of its bore in the camshaft carrier and keep it clean.

short: The computer that reads the transmission sensors and drives its solenoids to shift.
long: Short for transmission control module.

example.text: The TCM is matched to its transmission, which is why the routine asks for the serial number.

short: A diagnostic routine that tells a TCM which transmission it is paired with, using the transmission serial number.

example.text: Connect a battery support unit and the JLR diagnostic tool, update the TCM to the latest calibration, then run the TCM configuration routine, entering the transmission serial number when asked.

short: The highest point of a piston’s travel, where it stops and reverses.
long: Short for top dead center.

example.text: Looking for TDC marks, or turning the engine counter-clockwise to reach the marks.

short: Taking a unit apart in order, noting and labeling parts as they come off.

example.text: There is no pan to reach the filter from outside, so it is only changed during a teardown.

short: A sensor whose resistance changes with temperature, used to report coolant, oil, fluid or metal temperature.

example.text: Remove the cylinder head temperature sensor, the coolant pipe assembly and the coolant pipe at the head.

short: The fluid temperature range in which a level check or a learning procedure is valid.

example.text: The level is only correct with the engine running and the fluid in the temperature window.

short: A notched strip on a tensioner plunger that works like a ratchet, stopping the plunger being pushed back too far.

example.text: Compress the RH tensioner plunger and lock it with the 2.5 mm stopper pin, with the first rack notch engaged.

short: A heat-operated valve that keeps coolant in the engine until it warms up, then opens the way to the radiator.

example.text: Spin the water pump bearing, check the impeller, test the thermostat in heated water, and check the crank pulley, chain cover and pans for cracks.

short: A Japanese maker of sealants; Subaru specifies its numbered products, such as 1217G, as liquid gasket.
The valve at the air inlet that the accelerator opens to let more air in.

example.text: Loosen the captive bolts, lift off the plastic intake manifold with its throttle and manifold pressure (MAP) sensor, and discard the four port seals.

short: A push along the length of a shaft; on a piston, the sideways push that presses it against one side of the cylinder.

example.text: Measure each liner at four depths (10, 45, 80 and 115 mm) in both the thrust and pin directions and work out size, taper and out-of-round.

short: A bearing that takes push along a shaft’s length and limits how far the shaft can slide.

example.text: With all main bearings in the block and the crank laid in, measure end play at the number 5 thrust bearing with a feeler gauge.

short: A surface that takes an end-on or sideways push from a neighboring part.

example.text: Measure each piston across the thrust faces 13.3 mm up from the skirt bottom and subtract from its bore size.

short: A flat half-moon or ring washer that takes a shaft’s end-on push and sets its end play.

example.text: Place the two thrust washers on either side of the center main web, with their grooves facing the crank.

short: The set order for tightening or loosening a group of bolts, so a part is pulled down or released evenly.

example.text: Run the case bolts down and torque them to spec in a crossing pattern.

short: A metal link chain that drives the camshafts from the crankshaft so they stay exactly in step.

example.text: The timing chains sit at the transmission end, so the transmission and drive plate must come off before any chain work is possible.

short: A cast cover that encloses the timing chains and keeps their oil in.

example.text: Oil the bores, fit new O-rings and install both VCT solenoids into the upper timing cover.

short: Special tools that lock the crankshaft and camshafts in the timing position so the chains can be changed without losing timing.

example.text: Fit the crankshaft pulley locking tool to the front pulley and lock it in place.

short: Marks on the sprockets, crankshaft and covers that line up when the engine is correctly timed.

example.text: The pulley carries the timing mark and the locking tool needed for the timing steps.

short: The mark that marking compound leaves on gear teeth, showing where a pinion and ring gear actually meet.
The uppermost compression ring, nearest the heat of combustion.

example.text: Stand the block rear down on the four bolts, then clock each top ring gap to its mark and the second ring gap opposite it, seat the upper rail stopper in the side hole, set the expander gap opposite the upper rail and set the lower rail gap 120 degrees clockwise from the upper rail.

short: JLR’s technical information website for workshop manuals and service data.
A twisting force, like a wrench turning a bolt or an engine turning a shaft.
long: For bolts, the specified torque is the turning force used to tighten them. For engines and transmissions, it is how hard they can turn their output shaft.

example.text: Install the valve body bolts and torque them in sequence.

short: A sealed, fluid-filled coupling between engine and transmission that lets the car idle in gear and multiplies torque from a stop.

example.text: The stopper keeps the converter seated on the transmission input shaft as the engine pulls away.

short: A metal insert in a plastic part’s bolt hole that takes the clamp load so the plastic is not crushed.

example.text: Remove the cover bolts (they stay captive in their torque limiters) and lift off the ribbed plastic side cover with its molded seal.

short: A wrench that clicks or reads out when a set torque is reached.
A bolt tightened until it stretches slightly and permanently, which gives an even clamp load; it must not be reused.

example.text: These are torque-to-yield bolts, and oil in the blind holes gives false readings or can crack the block.

short: A six-pointed star shape for fasteners: T sizes are star-shaped holes in a bolt, and E sizes are star-shaped bolts that take a socket.
long: A T-size bit fits into the bolt. An E-size socket, also called an external Torx socket, fits over the outside of the bolt.

short: The Subaru Lineartronic CVT in the 2014 to 2018 Forester, one of the units in this app.

example.text: On the TR580 the forward clutch rides on the input shaft ahead of the primary pulley.

short: A larger, stronger Subaru CVT used with more powerful engines.

example.text: Using High Torque CVTF (meant for TR690 units such as the Forester XT) or a generic CVT fluid.

short: A clutch pack at the rear of the transmission that sends a varying share of drive to the rear wheels.

example.text: Measure transfer clutch clearance and use a different plate thickness until it is in range.

short: A gear that carries drive across from one shaft line to another, toward the differential or the rear wheels.

example.text: Reverse of removal: the transfer gear must be in before the differential can mesh with it.

short: The unit behind the engine that changes how fast the wheels turn compared with the engine, and passes the drive on.
long: An automatic picks its own gear; with a stick shift the driver picks it. Both transmissions in this app are automatics.

example.text: Once the bellhousing bolts are out, the transmission would otherwise drop on its rear mount.

short: The main aluminum housing that holds the transmission’s gears, shafts and hydraulics.

example.text: Install the external hydraulic line with new seals and bolt the TCM back onto the case.

short: The filter the fluid passes through on its way to the pump.
Mounted sideways across the car, with the crankshaft pointing left to right.
A pump with a lobed inner rotor turning inside a lobed outer rotor, squeezing oil along between them.
A numbered fault record a control module stores when it sees a problem, read with a code reader.

example.text: Read every TCM fault code, record the TCM software level, and note the transmission serial number before touching a wrench.

short: A maker’s notice to dealers about a known problem and its fix.
long: Short for technical service bulletin.

example.text: Upside-down compression rings pump oil into the chamber, the same symptom behind Subaru's FB oil consumption bulletins.

short: A seal where a fluid tube crosses the joint between two sections of a transmission case.

example.text: Leaving out the new tube seal between case and bell housing.

short: A flap in each intake runner that partly closes at low load so the air tumbles, helping a cold engine burn cleanly.

example.text: Unplug and unbolt the tumble generator valve assemblies from each head, then remove the cylinder head plates behind them.

short: A bladed wheel turned by flowing fluid or gas: the output wheel in a torque converter, or the exhaust wheel of a turbocharger.
The small pipes that bring oil to a turbocharger’s bearings and drain it back to the engine.

example.text: Remove the bolt and pull the turbo oil return pipe, discarding its two O-rings.

short: A wheel spun by the exhaust that drives a second wheel on the same shaft to pack more air into the engine.

example.text: The cooler sits under the turbo, so the turbo has to come off first.

short: A turbocharger whose housing has two separate exhaust inlets fed by paired cylinders, which helps it respond faster.
A connecting rod bent so that its two ends are turned against each other and no longer line up; checked along with bend.

example.text: Check each rod for bend and twist on a rod aligner and look over the thrust faces and small-end bushing.

short: A screw puller with two hooked arms that draws a bearing or gear off a shaft or boss.

example.text: Use a two-jaw puller seated in the case reliefs to pull the transfer gear bearing off its case boss, spacing the puller with a socket if needed.

short: Smaller than standard, as for a journal ground smaller; the matching bearing shells are made thicker to fit it.

example.text: JLR sizes clearances with graded bearings rather than undersize shells, so a reground crank needs non-factory bearings.

short: A threaded fitting that joins a pipe to a part or to another pipe.

example.text: Install the camshaft position sensors, oil temperature sensor, oil pressure switch and the oil pump union.

short: A change to a higher gear, or to a lower one.

example.text: Drive through every upshift to ninth and every downshift, including part-throttle and kickdown shifts, and check the engagements from Park to Reverse to Drive.

short: Steel blocks with a V-shaped notch that cradle a shaft so it can be turned and checked for bend or runout.

example.text: Check camshaft bend with a dial gauge on V-blocks, and measure lobe height, base circle and journal diameters.

short: Pulling a vacuum on the cooling system and letting it suck coolant in, so no air pockets are left.

example.text: Vacuum fill the cooling system and check for leaks at the pump, thermostat housing, oil cooler and turbo lines.

short: A pump that pulls air out to make a vacuum, here to power the brake booster.

example.text: Unplug the pump solenoid, remove the pickup pipe bolt and four pump bolts, and lift off the variable-flow oil pump with its vacuum pump.

short: Any part that opens, closes or steers a passage for air, gas, oil or fluid.
long: The word covers many different parts. The specific kinds, from the valves in the engine to the sliding valves in a transmission, have their own entries.

example.text: Turning the crank counterclockwise here can bring a piston up into an open valve.

short: A casting full of maze-like passages and spool valves, with solenoids attached, that sends fluid to the right clutches for each gear.

example.text: Subaru sells the valve body only as an assembly; the updated design fixes lock-up and shudder faults.

short: The cover over the valve body and its solenoids, on the top or side of the transmission.

example.text: Remove the cover bolts (they stay captive in their torque limiters) and lift off the ribbed plastic side cover with its molded seal.

short: The small gap between the cam and the parts it pushes while the valve is closed, so the valve can close fully when hot.

example.text: Each shim was selected for one valve; mixing them throws every cam clearance off.

short: The angled ring on the underside of a valve head that seals against the seat.

example.text: Inspect each valve face, stem and seat, and check the guides for wear by rocking each valve in its guide.

short: A tube pressed into the cylinder head that a valve stem slides in, keeping the valve centered on its seat.

example.text: JLR lists the valve guides as non-serviceable.

short: The thin flat edge around a valve head above its face; if it is too thin, the valve can burn.

example.text: Measure each valve stem and each guide bore in six places, subtract the stem diameter from the bore to get the clearance, and check the valve margin thickness.

short: The hard ring in the cylinder head that a closed valve presses against to seal.
A small hardened disc of chosen thickness that sets one valve’s clearance.

example.text: Lift out the RH roller rockers, O-rings, valve shims and rocker pivots and store each in a labeled tray by valve.

short: The coil spring that snaps a valve shut and keeps it following the cam.

example.text: Zero lift means no valve spring is pushing up while the carrier draws down.

short: A clamp that squeezes a valve spring so the collets can be removed or fitted.
The long, thin shaft of a valve that slides in its guide.

example.text: Measure each valve stem tip and the bore of its shim and confirm the clearance between them.

short: A small rubber seal on top of each valve guide that stops oil running down the stem.

example.text: Remove the valve stem seals from the guides, then remove the stud bolts and the chain cover bolt from the heads.

short: When each valve opens and closes, compared with the crankshaft’s position.

example.text: With the engine still in the vehicle, scan the engine computer (PCM) and save every stored code and the camshaft timing data.

short: The camshafts and every part between them and the valves.
A pump with sliding blades, called vanes, in a turning rotor that sweep fluid around and push it out under pressure.

example.text: Remove the pump drive chain and sprockets, noting their orientation, then lift the vane pump out of its pocket in the pump housing.

short: An oil pump whose output a solenoid can turn down when full pressure is not needed, saving fuel.

example.text: Unplug the pump solenoid, remove the pickup pipe bolt and four pump bolts, and lift off the variable-flow oil pump with its vacuum pump.

short: The two pulleys and the chain together: the part of a CVT that changes the ratio.

example.text: Break the sealant and lift the transmission case straight off the converter case, leaving the variator standing.

short: The heavy steel chain of plates and pins that runs between the two CVT pulleys, gripped by their sheaves.
A hard brown film left by overheated oil or fluid; drained fluid that smells of it has been cooked.

example.text: Pull the pan drain plug, catch the CVTF in a clean pan and look at it: metal glitter, a varnish smell or a milky look each point to a different failure.

short: Variable cam timing: JLR’s name for its cam phasers and their control.

example.text: With the locking tools still fitted, tighten both VCT center bolts to torque and then the final angle.

short: Vehicle identification number: the 17-character code that identifies one exact car.
How far a surface that should be flat has bent out of flat.

example.text: A warped head face will not clamp evenly even if every bolt is torqued correctly.

short: The coolant passages cast around the cylinders inside the block and head.

example.text: Only a light coat of oil goes on the bolts so none reaches the water jacket.

short: A plastic insert in the water jacket that steers coolant so the cylinder walls warm evenly.

example.text: Set the water jacket spacers into the RH and LH halves.

short: The pump that circulates coolant through the engine and radiator.

example.text: Hold the pulley, remove its three bolts, then remove the six pump bolts and the coolant pump.

short: A small hole on a water pump that drips coolant when the pump’s internal seal starts to fail.
A plate under the crankshaft that stops the spinning crank whipping up the oil; some also stiffen the block.

example.text: Remove the bolts and the cast aluminum structural windage tray from the bottom of the block.

short: The bundle of wires, connectors and clips that links the control modules to every sensor and actuator.

example.text: Lay the engine harness back on, reconnect every connector, and install the generator.

short: The wrench or socket size a bolt needs, measured across the flats of its hex, not the size of its thread.
A camshaft position where every valve it works is on its base circle and closed.

example.text: Every cam must sit at zero lift before the cam carriers are unbolted, or spring pressure loads the carrier unevenly.

short: The German maker of the nine-speed automatic in the Discovery Sport.
long: Full name: ZF Friedrichshafen.

example.text: Mate the engine to the ZF 9HP48 transmission and refit the powertrain to the vehicle following the vehicle procedures.
